new_entities.name: Microneedling adjunct to topical minoxidil
new_entities.description: Scalp microneedling used alongside topical minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia.

new_entities.name: Androgenetic alopecia
aliases: male or female pattern hair loss
new_entities.description: Progressive androgen-mediated scalp hair loss in men or women.

edges.effect_quant: When microneedling is added to topical minoxidil, pooled trial data usually show better hair-density and global-response outcomes than minoxidil alone.
edges.mechanism: Microneedling may improve delivery of topical agents and trigger wound-healing pathways that stimulate follicular signaling and stem-cell activity in the scalp. The key point is that the best evidence is for adjunctive use with minoxidil, not for a proven standalone microneedling effect.
edges.summary: The evidence here is promising but more specific than it first sounds. Meta-analyses of randomized trials generally show that adding microneedling to topical minoxidil improves hair-related outcomes compared with minoxidil alone, which makes it a plausible adjunctive therapy rather than a universally proven monotherapy.
edges.caveats: Protocols differ widely across studies in needle depth, frequency, and accompanying topical regimens. Because most of the evidence is combination-based, this edge should not be stretched into a claim that microneedling alone is equally well supported.
